metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [24. November 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.184

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [24. November 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.184
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.184
- Datum: 24.11.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
24. Nov. 1941 Dear Hannah & Manfred, now the black day is very near and
we will pass it not at home but on a excursion to a little place in the
country; I have asked all my friends not to mention it in the newspapers
(where even the birthdays of children are printed with an overflow of pa-
thetic phrases) and it is better to be away. We feel here already somewhat
at home, Lotte is much better and we wait for the summer which will be
delicious here as one escapes the hot nights and has all the day open
door life (we live since months with open windows also the doors are
not locked when we go away, - patriarchal times.) - About Eva we had
news from Newyork. It was a misfortune that Mr Schaeffer broke her
arm just now, where she was necessary for the new installation and we all
live somewhat in the provisory, why not Eva and it is perhaps good, that
she learns in time how to overcome little difficulties. She was over weekend
with my
sister-in-law, who has the best intentions; unfortunately they are both,
my brother and she, somewhat pathological with her continuous fever. He
in comparison with
- [?] I was even in my best times a poor man - has fear to
die as a beggar (and they have no children!) she cooks and washes, while
all others find servants - I am so sorry that they are as they are and
much would have been easier also for me if they would be otherwise,
but she is at least willing to do something while on the others one
cannot rely. (all people have their worries there and everyone is gifted
with at least ten refugee-relatives) I am glad that Mr. Breuer invited
her and she had lunch at her father, the great Morgenthau (on gold and
silver plates) of course we wish she had somebody who is her real friend
in Newyork and I would be glad, if my sister in law would be at least
to her with all her awkwardness - my dear, how easy life would be if
people were quite normal, but I am not sure to be it myself. If one would
leave her longer with my sister in law she would wrap her in flannels and
give her medicine all day (they have killed three dogs by giving them
constant medicine and at the smallest cold they want go to doctors and
specialists - her neurotic fear exaggerates everything and it would
not be a good milieu for Eva; on the other hand I am glad that there
is somebody who cares for her as unfortunately we are away. So do not
worry about her, she is in best health and good spirits, Lites [?] her home, her aunt Olga and
her school; Kate the most important except that she is really longing for you
secretly as you are doing quite openly. Yours Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Die Transkription umfasst auch die Randnotizen, die sich über den linken und rechten Rand erstrecken.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der Randnotizen. Einige wenige Wörter sind aufgrund der kursiven Handschrift leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext eindeutig.
